# David Packer Recommends Weighted Pull-Ups At About 50 Of Your Body Weight For About Three To Five Reps As A Front Lever Prerequisite

David Packer recommends aiming for weighted pull-ups at about 50 of your body weight for about three to five reps as a prerequisite to achieve a front lever hold. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Details

- If a 75 kg person can do 40 kg weighted pull-ups for about three to five reps, they can likely do a front lever for two seconds even with sagging hips. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- After achieving the two-second front lever from weighted pull-ups, he recommends starting front lever raises to inverted hang rather than using heavy bands or front lever pull-ups. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Evidence

- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "go for weighted pull-ups aim for about 50 of your body weight and shoot for about five reps so if you're say 75 kilograms if you can if you can do 40 kilogram weighted pull-ups for about three to five reps i i can almost guarantee you can do a front lever for two seconds"
